World.title: When the voice of humanity reverberated in a man, By Owei Lakemfa
World.content:
“In a world where selfishness, war, and injustice are resurgent, Fidel’s legacy calls upon us to: defend the sovereignty of peoples against any form of domination; practice internationalist solidarity; work towards and trust in unity as an invincible force; and foster values of justice and ethics.” …In Cuba itself, the First International Colloquium on the Centenary held with the theme “Fidel: Legacy and Future.” It brought together over 1,500 participants, including over 900 international delegates from sixty-three countries. This week across the world, the voice of humanity reverberated in one man, Fidel Castro, the revolutionary they could not kill.

Across the world, countries, movements and groups on Thursday 13 August marked the centenary of Fidel Castro Ruz, the iconic Cuban revolutionary. That was yesterday. But Fidel is not yesterday’s man. Although he marched into the full embrace of history on 25 November, 2016, he is a man of today, as his ideas of a better humanity and world, continue to spread. Given their timeless nature, Fidel will be also be a man of tomorrow. In Nigeria, we gathered at the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Africa’s largest labour centre, for his commemoration.

Joined by workers, professionals political, human rights activists, and ambassadors of various countries, we filled its conference hall, flowing to the upper chambers, as various participants took the audiences through the essential Fidel Castro. For me, at the occasion, I was more interested in Fidel, the humanist, who despite the famed efficiency of the United States’ (US) Central Intelligence Agency, survived over six hundred assassination plots by that agency. I reflected that when Fidel spoke on arrival in Havana at the beginning of the Cuban Revolution, a dove flew around and perched on its shoulder, as if saying, this is the chosen one. I recalled that when he died, a big all-night African funeral ceremony was held for him by groups of Nigerians at the National Stadium, Lagos, as they saw him as an African ancestor. These I narrated at this occasion.

The National Chairperson of the Nigeria Solidarity Movement with Cuba, Salisu Nuhu Mohammed, said Fidel was one of the most outstanding personalities of the Twentieth Century. Fidel, he pointed out, dedicated his life to a better humanity and led the first successful revolution in the Western hemisphere. He described Cuba as a small country which has withstood US’ challenges and pressures, from which almost all other countries would have collapsed. Mohammed, who has been a member of the Cuban Solidarity Movement for over four decades, observed that today Cuba faces a most inhuman blockade by the US, designed to, “deny Cubans oxygen.” But the American leaders will fail because, “They may wake up very early, but the Cuban Revolution does not sleep.” He added that, “Cuba has shown Africa solidarity, it is now time for Africa to show Cuba solidarity.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

NLC President Joe Ajaero said the Congress has been inspired by great thinkers like Fidel Castro and has not departed from the cause which they stood for. Represented by Comrade Eche Asuzu, head of Industrial Relations and Organising of the Congress, Ajaero called on the US and its allies to lift their boots off the necks of the Cuban people, adding that Cubans have a right to determine their future.

Ambassador Brahim S Busseif of the Saharawi Arab Democratic Republic (SADR), better known as Western Sahara, said Fidel was a great leader and leader of international solidarity. He recalled that when Morocco used napalm bomb against the Saharawi, Fidel sent medical aid. Busseif submitted that the legacy of Fidel will continue to be celebrated, no matter the odds.

The Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC), which, next to the NLC, is the largest labour centre in Africa, said the occasion is a solemn one as Cubans are being forced to go through a nightmare by the US. It said that as a direct consequence of the US actions, including denying Cuba access to fuel and electricity, thousands of Cuban children have died since the tightening of the US blockade on 29 January. Represented by Comrade Martins Egbanubi, the labour centre said the Fidel Centenary tells the world that it needs unity because all are vulnerable to American attacks. “In the trade union movement it is time for us to rethink and re-strategise, don’t say it is not happening to you today. The time to solidarise with Cuba is now,” he declared.

Egbanubi recalled that Cuba has made tremendous progress in various areas, especially Medicine and, sent medical teams across the world to help humanity. He gave the example of Cuba producing COVID-19 vaccines and distributing them free to other countries. The TUC said it is time for the United Nations to go beyond resolutions and hold the US responsible for crimes against Cuba. It added that, “It is time for the world to rise to the defence of humanity.”

Senator Shehu Sani used the occasion to pay tributes to one of the greatest Fidelistas in Nigeria, Comrade Abiodun ‘Aremson’ Aremu, who departed on 10 October, 2025. The Senator warned that, “If Cuba falls, we all fall.” He argued that Cuba is the test of our collective morality, integrity and “our humanity.” He said the charges that US brought against veteran Cuban revolutionary and former President Raul Castro are bogus and designed to persecute him and the Cuban people. He told African leaders that the African people have never had a better friend than Cuba. He promised that if he wins the 2027 Kaduna Central Senatorial election, he would introduce a bill on the Cuban situation.

Ambassador Brahim S Busseif of the Saharawi Arab Democratic Republic (SADR), better known as Western Sahara, said Fidel was a great leader and leader of international solidarity. He recalled that when Morocco used napalm bomb against the Saharawi, Fidel sent medical aid. Busseif submitted that the legacy of Fidel will continue to be celebrated, no matter the odds.

Labour internationalist, Baba Aye…talked about how Fidel’s ideas influenced Nigerian students and inspired popular songs like “Freedom comes by struggle.” He recalled that Fidel inspired the establishment of solidarity movements like the Tricontinental, adding that, “Cuba has been there for the working class, now, we have to be there for Cuba.”

Veteran human rights activist and columnist, Aminu Habibu Jahun, who travelled all the way from Jigawa State, said he was fortunate to have been exposed to the ideas of Fidel when he was a student. He submitted that the current US aggression against Cuba is because it had failed to kill Fidel. The Nigeria-Cuba Graduates Association, through its President Dr Audu Onuche, issued a Declaration on the unquantifiable contributions of Fidel to medicine, especially the training of doctors from various continents. Labour internationalist, Baba Aye, who is visiting from Europe, talked about how Fidel’s ideas influenced Nigerian students and inspired popular songs like “Freedom comes by struggle.” He recalled that Fidel inspired the establishment of solidarity movements like the Tricontinental, adding that, “Cuba has been there for the working class, now, we have to be there for Cuba.”

Cuban Ambassador Miriam Morales Palmero told the audience the year-long celebration “serves to reaffirm our respect for and unwavering commitment to the ideals and example of a man who championed the banners of independence and sovereignty, as well as respect and dignity for humanity.” The Cuban Ambassador added that, “In a world where selfishness, war, and injustice are resurgent, Fidel’s legacy calls upon us to: defend the sovereignty of peoples against any form of domination; practice internationalist solidarity; work towards and trust in unity as an invincible force; and foster values of justice and ethics.”

In Cuba itself, the First International Colloquium on the Centenary held with the theme “Fidel: Legacy and Future.” It brought together over 1,500 participants, including over 900 international delegates from sixty-three countries. This week across the world, the voice of humanity reverberated in one man, Fidel Castro, the revolutionary they could not kill.

Owei Lakemfa, a former secretary general of African workers, is a human rights activist, journalist and author.

World.title: Osun election: Political parties engage in vote buying in Ikire
World.content:
By Dapo Akinrefon

Agents of the Accord Party and the All Progressives Congress, APC, were seen engaged in vote buying at AUD Primary School in Atile, Ikire, Irewole Local Government Area of Osun State.

Vanguard observed that party agents stationed themselves around the polling booths to monitor the voters.

The move is to monitor voters and their ballot papers to ensure they cast their votes for their candidate.

It was further observed that as soon as a voter casts his or her vote, a party agent hands over a tag to enable the voter to claim their cash.

An Accord Party agent, Ajayi Ayodele, was seen accusing APC agents of clustering around the polling booths to monitor the ballot papers.

Aside from the APC, the ruling party (Accord Party) was also engaged in vote buying as he was seen directing voters to a destination after voting to collect their funds.

Security agents, Vanguard observed, were unable to curb the party agents’ activities.

A security agent, whose name was withheld, lamented that he had tried to prevent the agents from loitering around the polling booths, but his efforts proved abortive.

World.title: Ghana Police kill two, arrest Nigerian over alleged bank robbery attempt
World.content:
The Ghana Police Service say they have arrested a Nigerian identified as Augustine Okechuku Maazi and killed two other suspected members of a robbery gang during an intelligence-led operation in Accra.

The police said the operation, which took place on Thursday, foiled an alleged plan by a robbery syndicate to attack banks in the Labone area of Accra.

According to a statement by the Police Service, it received intelligence at about 10:45am that the gang was preparing to attack GCB Bank, Ecobank and Zenith Bank in the area.

A response team was subsequently deployed to Labone, where officers reportedly found members of the suspected gang in vehicles parked close to the banks.

The police said one of the vehicles sped away after the suspects noticed the officers, prompting the operatives to give chase. Maazi was eventually arrested, while another occupant of the vehicle escaped.

According to the police, occupants of a second vehicle also attempted to flee while firing at the officers.

“The robbers in the second vehicle also tried to escape amidst firing, but the police engaged them in a shootout, resulting in the death of two suspects,” the Police Service stated.

The police added that a fourth suspect escaped during the operation and that a manhunt had been launched to apprehend him.

Following the operation, the police said two vehicles allegedly linked to the suspects were recovered. They included a Toyota Highlander with registration number GS-1434-18 and a Hyundai Tucson with registration number GS 7915-17.

A blow pistol was also reportedly recovered.

The Police Service said Maazi remained in custody and was assisting investigators with the ongoing investigation.

The bodies of the two deceased suspects, it added, had been deposited at the morgue for preservation, identification and autopsy.

The police urged members of the public to continue providing credible information about suspected criminal activities to security authorities.

However, GCB Bank has denied that its Labone branch was robbed or that an attempted robbery occurred on its premises.

In a statement issued following the police announcement, the bank said neither its premises nor its operations were breached during the incident.

GCB said no customer, employee, funds or property belonging to the bank was affected.

The police have not disclosed whether the alleged plot involved an attempt to enter any of the banks or target customers and other persons in the surrounding area.

World.title: ‘You all feed off Nigerians pain’ — Sowore blasts Davido, Adeleke family in war of words
World.content:
Award-winning Nigerian singer Davido and human rights activist Omoyele Sowore have engaged in a heated exchange on social media following comments about Ademola Adeleke, the Osun State governor and Davido’s uncle.

The disagreement began after Sowore criticised Adeleke during a recent interview on the forthcoming Osun governorship election.

In the interview, Sowore described the governor as “brainless” and said he had “nothing upstairs”. He also criticised the state of infrastructure in Osogbo, the state capital, describing the city as a “war zone”.

Davido later shared a clip of the interview on X and responded by calling Sowore an “Arindin”, a Yoruba term used to describe someone considered foolish or unintelligent.

Sowore subsequently responded to Davido, arguing that the description was more appropriate for Adeleke.

The activist also criticised the governor’s political record, particularly his decision to support President Bola Tinubu during the 2023 presidential election.

Sowore further accused the Adeleke family of treating Osun as a “private estate” to finance their lifestyle, describing them as “oppressive, corrupt, incompetent, and entitled”.

Responding directly to Davido, Sowore wrote: “The real arindin is your uncle, @AAdeleke_01, who had to go back and obtain the equivalent of a GED after he had already served as a Nigerian Senator,”

He added: “The real arindin is your uncle who chose @officialABAT as his presidential candidate, apparently hoping that imbecilic political loyalty would allow your family to continue treating Osun state as a private estate to finance your extravagant lifestyle.

“All of you are the same anyway, oppressive, corrupt, incompetent, and entitled spoilt brats, feeding off the pain, suffering, and sorrow of Nigerians. But the tables will turn. The Nigerian people will not endure this forever.”

World.title: Osun Election: Panic in Modakeke as alleged policemen cart away materials

“All the election agents and corps members took to their heels as soon as they arrived,” the witness said.

The circumstances surrounding the incident, including the identity of those who allegedly took away the materials, could not be independently verified as of the time of filing this report.

There was also no immediate official statement from the police or the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) on the reported incident.

World.title: Only 3 countries have won the WAFCON in history – see list
World.content:
Nigeria remain the most successful team in the history of the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), having won the continental championship a record 10 times.

The Super Falcons claimed their latest title in 2025 after producing a remarkable comeback to defeat hosts Morocco 3-2 in the final, extending their dominance in African women’s football.

Since the tournament was first held in 1991, only three countries have lifted the WAFCON trophy: Nigeria, Equatorial Guinea and South Africa.

The competition, which is traditionally held every two years, has been dominated by Nigeria, who have won the majority of the titles.

Equatorial Guinea have won the tournament twice, while South Africa have one championship to their name.

1. Nigeria – 10 titles

Titles: 1998, 2000, 2002, 2004, 2006, 2010, 2014, 2016, 2018, 2025

Nigeria’s Super Falcons are comfortably the most successful team in WAFCON history, with 10 titles to their name.

Their first official triumph came in 1998 when they defeated Ghana 2-0 in the final on home soil. They successfully defended the title two years later with another 2-0 victory, this time against hosts South Africa.

Nigeria went on to beat Ghana in the 2002 final, before defeating Cameroon 5-0 in 2004 and Ghana 1-0 in 2006.

After failing to win the 2008 edition, the Super Falcons returned to the top in 2010, beating Equatorial Guinea 4-2 in the final.

They added further titles in 2014, 2016 and 2018. Their 2018 triumph came after a goalless final against South Africa, with Nigeria winning 4-3 on penalties.

Nigeria then produced one of the most memorable comebacks in WAFCON history in 2025, overturning a two-goal deficit to defeat Morocco 3-2 in the final and secure their 10th continental crown.

The Super Falcons also hold several tournament records, including the most WAFCON wins, appearances and goals scored.

2. Equatorial Guinea – 2 titles

Titles: 2008, 2012

Equatorial Guinea are the only other team to have won the WAFCON more than once.

They made history in 2008 by becoming the first country other than Nigeria to lift the trophy. Playing at home, Equatorial Guinea defeated South Africa 2-1 in the final after eliminating defending champions Nigeria in the semi-finals.

Four years later, the National Nzalang claimed their second title on home soil.

They defeated Cameroon 2-0 in the semi-final before recording a convincing 4-0 victory over South Africa in the final to become two-time African champions.

3. South Africa – 1 title

Title: 2022

South Africa finally ended years of near misses by winning their maiden WAFCON title in 2022.

Banyana Banyana had previously finished runners-up on five occasions before finally breaking their duck in Morocco.

They defeated the hosts 2-1 in the final in Rabat to claim their first continental championship.

Despite the growing competitiveness of women’s football across Africa, the WAFCON trophy has remained in the hands of just three nations since the competition began.

Full list of WAFCON winners

Nigeria – 10 titles Equatorial Guinea – 2 titles South Africa – 1 title
